Three docblocks were stacked above `crewPlan` in `legalActions.ts`: `manaSources`', the convoke
planner's, and `crewPlan`'s own. Only the last of the three documented the function under it —
TypeScript and every editor attach the *immediately* preceding comment, so the other two had been
documenting nothing since whenever a function was moved past them. Both are now directly above the
function they describe. Worth recording because it is a failure mode a reviewer cannot see: the
prose is present, correct, and attached to the wrong thing.

### The break harness, and a fourth defective test row — the same defect as D551's

10 of 10 caught, again after a correction. The first run came back **9/10**, and the survivor was
break 5: `available.push({ id, colors: ch.colors as readonly ManaType[] })`, which hands an
improvising artifact its real colours and so lets it pay a coloured pip.

The reason nothing caught it is the reason D551's survivor went uncaught, one increment later and
in a different file: **every artifact on the board in that block was colourless.** Tormod's Crypt is
`colors: []`, so `colors: []` and `ch.colors` are the same list and the coloured-pip test could not
tell the correct planner from the broken one. The row read like the heart of the mechanic and
asserted nothing about it.

Fixed by putting a **red** artifact on the board — Slagdrill Scrapper (`{R}`, Artifact Creature —
Robot Scout, 1/2, whose printed ability costs `{2}` and taps, so it is not a mana ability and never
enters `manaSources`). Against `{3}{R}` with no red land: generic-only refuses the `{R}`, convoke's
arm would pay it. Both boards are kept, with the docblock saying which one discriminates and which
one passes either way, because the colourless row still says something true (four artifacts are not
four mana) and deleting it would lose that.

**The generalised lesson, now twice confirmed:** a test about colour needs an object that *has* a
colour, and the default object in Magic — a colourless artifact, a colourless creature — is exactly
the one that makes such a test vacuous. Both survivors were quantifier-or-colour bugs whose
witnesses had empty colour lists. That is now a thing to check when writing the test rather than
when reading the harness output.

## D553 — A permanent that makes mana is tapped last, and a failing test is what found it

The Sol Ring row of D552's table block failed on first run, and it was the code that was wrong
rather than the test.

A Sol Ring is both an artifact improvise may tap and a source for `{C}{C}`, and it cannot be both.
Against a `{5}` spell with a Sol Ring and three Tormod's Crypts on the board, one assignment is
castable and the other is short by one:

- Ring tapped for mana (2) + three Crypts improvised (3) = **5**. Castable.
- Ring improvised (1) + three Crypts improvised (3) = **4**. Not castable.

The planner walked the battlefield in order, so it took whatever came first — and on that board
that was the Ring. The offer was refused for a board that could pay.

The fix is one sort and one sentence of reasoning:

```ts
const makesMana = new Set(sources.map((source) => source.key));
available.sort((a, b) => Number(makesMana.has(a.id)) - Number(makesMana.has(b.id)));
```

**Nothing is lost by the rule**, which is what makes it the right one rather than a heuristic.
Every mana pays a generic pip, so a permanent that makes mana is worth *at least* as much tapped
for mana as tapped for a cost: there is no board on which reaching for it first helps. A source
that makes one mana is worth exactly the same either way, which is why **convoke's own answers do
not move** — the pool's convoke tests, Llanowar Elves included, give the same counts before and
after, and that is why the rule can live in the shared planner rather than in one arm of it.

The latent form of this was in convoke from #101: a creature tapping for two mana would have had
the same problem, and the pool simply has no such creature. It took a mechanic whose fodder is
*artifacts* — where two-mana rocks are ordinary — to produce a board that discriminates. Another
entry for the standing lesson that a mechanic generalised is a mechanic tested from a new angle.

## D554 — Flanking, read by adding one word to a list

The keyword audit's next cheap row: 12 finishes, 27 printings. It needed **no reader at all**. The
word went into `KEYWORDS`, `isPrintedAbilityLine` claimed the line before `keywordScriptFor` was
ever asked, and one function in `combat.ts` enforces it:

```ts
export function flankingPenalties(state, attacks, defender): GameState
```

called by `declareBlockers` once the declaration is settled: every blocker **without flanking**
that blocked a flanker gets -1/-1 until end of turn (CR 702.25a).

### Why a keyword and a combat function rather than a trigger

In the rules this is a triggered ability. It is not one here, and the reason is the sentence's
own subordinate clause: "a creature **without flanking**". That is a question about the *blocker*,
and the only thing in this engine that can answer it is `characteristicsOf(...).keywords`. A
per-card trigger could emit the penalty and could not ask the question — so granted flanking
(Jabari's Banner, Agility), tribal flanking (Sidewinder Sliver) and lost flanking (Barbed Foliage)
would all be invisible to it. Myriad is in that list for exactly this reason, and this follows it.

**What it costs, stated rather than hidden:** the penalty lands as part of the block declaration
instead of going on the stack, so a player cannot answer the trigger itself — only the
declaration. The board is the same either way; the -1/-1 is in place before damage, which is the
point of the keyword. It is in the player cheat sheet in those words.

**Not represented:** cumulative flanking (CR 702.25b). A `ReadonlySet` cannot hold a count. No
legal card prints the line twice (measured), so nothing in this pool can tell.

### Measured — a keyword row that behaved like a vocabulary change

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| printed legal lines read | 23,583 (41.8%) | **23,614 / 56,421 (41.9%)** |
| cards with every printed line read | 7,851 | **7,866** |

Audit: 12 finishes, 27 printings. Delivered **15 and 31**. The extra four lines are the word being
consumed in more than one printed shape — two mixed lists ("Flying; flanking", "Protection from
black; flanking") and two grants (Jabari's Banner, Agility), which read because every grant reader
asks `isKeyword` and the answer changed. So the calibration rule gains a clause: the audit's
column is exact for a keyword read by a **reader**, and a floor for one read by joining a **list**,
because a list is shared vocabulary.

Sidewinder Sliver's "All Sliver creatures have flanking" is **not** read and is pinned unread by a
test, because the first draft of the `KEYWORDS` note claimed the grants "come along" without
having measured which ones. Two do and one does not.

### A stale refusal, retargeted (D516 again)

`refuses a word the engine has no keyword for` used **flanking** as its example of such a word. It
failed the moment flanking stopped being one, which is that test working. *Phasing* stands in now:
a keyword the rules define and nothing here models.

### The harness got faster, and stopped being dangerous

`break-par.py` replaces the per-increment serial harnesses. Three changes, each for a reason:

- **The real tree is never touched.** Each worker patches a private mirror of the engine package
  under the scratchpad. The serial harness patched tracked files and reverted them, which meant a
  commit made while it ran could pick up a deliberately broken file — the stop hook asked for
  exactly that commit during D552, and the only safe answer was to wait 25 minutes.
- **Two breaks run at once.** Vitest is capped at two workers a run and the box has four cores,
  so the serial harness left half the machine idle.
- **A catch has to name a failed test.** Under load a run can exit non-zero on a reporter timeout
  with every test passing, and a "caught" on that evidence would *hide* an uncaught break. So exit
  0 is uncaught, a parsed `N failed` is caught, and anything else — or a catch whose failures
  include a timeout — is re-run alone before it is believed. It also prints which test caught each
  break, which no earlier harness reported and which is the evidence D551 and D552 both lacked.

## D555 — Combat damage dealt as poison is still combat damage dealt

Found by reading `hit` in `combat.ts` to see where toxic would go.

That function records "this creature dealt combat damage to that player" — the fact every
"whenever ~ deals combat damage to a player" trigger is raised from — and it recorded it **only if
the life total moved**. Infect's damage to a player is poison instead of life (CR 702.90b). So an
infect creature's hit moved no life, was never recorded, and **its damage triggers never fired**.

The rule is the other way round: the damage is dealt, and infect changes only what being dealt it
does (CR 120.3b). `dealDamage`'s own commander-damage tally already said so two hundred lines
away — "the damage is dealt either way" — and `hit` did not agree with it.

```ts
if (after.life >= before.life && after.poison <= before.poison) return next;
```

**Who it affected.** Whispering Specter prints infect and a damage trigger on one card. More to
the point for Commander, so does *anything* handed infect: a Tainted Strike, a Grafted
Exoskeleton, a Triumph of the Hordes on a board of creatures with damage triggers. That is most of
the reason those cards are played.

**Reproduced before it was fixed.** Two pool cards, no printed rows: Thieving Magpie draws on a
hit and Tainted Strike gives it infect. The control row (ordinary hit, one life, one card) passed;
the poison row read `drew: 0` against an expected 1, with the two poison counters in place. After
the fix both rows pass.

In the engine since infect shipped (#138). The whole suite never asked, because no pool creature
*prints* both halves and no test had combined a grant with a trigger.

## D556 — Toxic N, the first printed ability that is a number

40 legal lines, 13 cards finished — **the audit's figure exactly**, the fourth keyword row to land
on it (evoke 18, renown 12, improvise 14, toxic 13).

"Players dealt combat damage by this creature also get N poison counters" (CR 702.164a).

### Not a `Keyword`, not a trigger

A `ReadonlySet<Keyword>` cannot say how much, and toxic is nothing but how much. Bushido met that
wall and went round it as a pair of triggers — right for bushido, which **is** a triggered ability
(CR 702.45a). Toxic is a static ability: the counters arrive *with* the damage. As a trigger there
would be a stack object and a round of priority where the rules have neither, and a player on nine
poison would die a pass later than they should.

So it is a printed part (`{ kind: 'toxic', amount }`), a base characteristic
(`Characteristics.toxic`, cleared by "loses all abilities" with the others, CR 613.1f), and one
block in `hit` — the single place that already knows the three facts the sentence needs: the
damage was **combat** damage, it went to a **player**, and it **landed**. Read off the board as
the damage was dealt, so a creature that died to the same simultaneous damage still gives its
poison.

Summed, not maxed: CR 702.164b. No legal card prints two instances, so the sum has one term today
and a test says it guards the rule rather than a printing.

### The tests take the three conditions one at a time

Every creature in the block has a toxic value **different from its power**, because a test where
the two are equal cannot tell poison-per-hit from poison-per-damage — which is the whole
difference between this keyword and infect. (The lesson from D551 and D552, applied while writing
rather than after the harness.)

- a 3-power Toxic 2 hits for three life **and** two poison;
- blocked: nothing, a creature is not a player;
- a 0/2 Toxic 1 Ornithopter connects for zero: nothing, zero damage is not dealt (CR 120.8);
- under a Fog: nothing;
- a player on eight poison dies as the hit lands, with an empty stack.

### Measured

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| printed legal lines read | 23,614 (41.9%) | **23,651 / 56,421 (41.9%)** |
| cards with a compiled script | 12,051 | **12,051** |
| cards with every printed line read | 7,866 | **7,879** |

The compiled-script count does not move for either of these two rows, and that is correct rather
than a miss: a line read off the `CardDef` emits no script. "Fully read" is the number that says
what a player gets.

## D557 — Mentor, Afterlife N and Rampage N: three rows on one cycle

Three keyword rows read together because the engine already had every part of all three, and
because the fixed cost of an increment — a gate, a break run, a pod sweep, two progress entries —
is the same for one row as for three.

| keyword | rule | what it was built from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Mentor** (CR 702.133a) | whenever this attacks, +1/+1 counter on target attacking creature with lesser power | Sunhome Stalwart's own trigger, moved behind `mentorTrigger()` so the pool card and the compiled reading are the same code — renown's arrangement (D549) |
| **Afterlife N** (CR 702.135a) | when this dies, create N 1/1 white and black Spirit tokens with flying | a `dies` trigger and `createToken` |
| **Rampage N** (CR 702.23a) | when this becomes blocked, +N/+N until end of turn for each blocker beyond the first | the batched `blocked-creature` event and `pump` |

All three are genuinely triggered abilities, so unlike flanking and toxic they read in
`keywordScriptFor` and use the stack as the rules do.

### Two details that were decisions

**The afterlife Spirit is its own token definition.** The pool already has a `SPIRIT_TOKEN` — a
*white* 1/1 flier, the one Doomed Traveler leaves. Afterlife's is **white and black**, which a
"nonblack" removal spell and a protection-from-black creature can both see. Both are named
"Spirit", and token definitions are keyed by name, so the second kind to arrive would have
recoloured the first. It is registered under its own key, and a test kills one of each in a single
game and checks the board holds `['BW', 'BW', 'W']`.

**Rampage reads the batched event, not the per-blocker one.** `becomes-blocked` fires once per
blocker and would count the whole gang each time; `blocked-creature` fires once however many
blocked. That is D482's finding on Ichorclaw Myr and bushido's choice, made a third time.

### Measured — the audit exact on three rows at once

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| printed legal lines read | 23,651 (41.9%) | **23,689 / 56,421 (42.0%)** |
| cards with a compiled script | 12,051 | **12,082** |
| cards with every printed line read | 7,879 | **7,903** |

Predicted 8 + 7 + 9 = **24** finishes and 18 + 11 + 9 = **38** printings. Delivered **24** and
**38**. Seven keyword rows have now been read through a *reader* (evoke, renown, improvise, toxic
and these three) and all seven landed on the audit's figure exactly; the two that beat it —
D551's clause vocabulary and flanking's `KEYWORDS` entry — were both changes to something shared.

### A test-helper mistake worth keeping

The first draft of the rampage rows read the Berserker as a 2/4 against two and three blockers —
the mechanic apparently doing nothing on exactly the board it exists for. The trigger was fine. Two
or more blockers owe the attacking player a **damage assignment order** (CR 509.2), priority does
not return until it is given, and the helper never gave it, so the trigger sat on the stack
unresolved. Third entry for the lesson that began with `drain` not advancing a step: when a combat
test reads a trigger as inert, ask what the table is waiting for before asking what the card did.

### Addendum to D554 and D556 — the second and third harness runs

**D555 and D556: 10 of 10 caught on the first run**, each catch naming the test that defends it.
That is the first increment this session whose tests needed no correction after the harness, and
the reason is not luck: the toxic rows were written with the D551/D552 lesson in hand — every
creature has a toxic value different from its power, so no row can pass for a reason other than
its own.

**D554's duration break took three runs to catch, and the second miss was a real one.** The first
run had no duration test at all. The second had one and *still* passed against a permanent
penalty: it sent a 1/1 flanker into a 3/3 blocker, the flanker died, and an effect whose source
has left the battlefield is cleaned up regardless of its duration — so the blocker was restored
next turn for a reason that had nothing to do with "until end of turn". The row now uses a 2/2
Cavalry into a 2/4 Giant Spider, where both creatures survive and the duration is the only thing
that can restore the Spider.

That is the fifth vacuous row the harness has found in four increments, and the fourth distinct
way of being vacuous: a second restriction on the same card (D551), an empty colour list (D551,
D552), and now **a second mechanism producing the asserted outcome**. The common shape is worth
more than the list: a test is vacuous whenever something other than the code under test can
produce what it asserts, and the cheapest check for that is to break the code and see whether
the test notices.

### Break harness for D557: 13 of 13

Twelve breaks for the three keywords and the D554 duration break on its third attempt, all caught
on the first run of this spec — the "lesser, not equal" mentor filter, the afterlife count, the
white-versus-two-coloured token, the registry-key collision, rampage's off-by-one in both
directions and its per-blocker event, and both end anchors. 22 minutes for thirteen full-suite
runs on two mirrors, against roughly 33 serially.

## D558 — Bloodthirst N, and the fact "was dealt damage this turn"

**Bloodthirst N** (CR 702.54a): "If an opponent was dealt damage this turn, this creature enters
with N +1/+1 counters on it." 21 legal cards print it with a number; the keyword audit ranked it
the largest remaining row whose parts the engine mostly had.

It had all but one. `entersWith` already puts counters on a permanent as its spell resolves, and
bloodthirst is that replacement with a condition in front of it. The condition is the new part.

### The fact is damage, and the engine only remembered life

`lifeLostThisTurn` (spectacle's fact, D197) was the obvious thing to reuse and it is the wrong
one, in both directions:

| what happened to the opponent | life lost this turn | dealt damage this turn | bloodthirst |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shocked for 2 | yes | yes | **on** |
| drained by Zulaport Cutthroat | yes | no | **off** |
| hit by an infect creature | no | yes (CR 702.90b: the damage is dealt, its result is poison) | **on** |

So there is a second record, `GameState.damagedThisTurn`, written by `recordDamaged` at the one
place a player is dealt damage (`dealDamage`'s player path, after both the infect branch and the
life branch) and cleared with the turn's other records at cleanup. It is optional on the state so
a snapshot saved before today still loads, and read only through `damagedThisTurn(state, seat)`,
which answers zero for such a snapshot. Prevented damage never reaches the record: it is written
with what was left after prevention, and zero writes nothing.

### Where the condition is asked

As the permanent arrives, beside `entersWith` — not when the spell is cast. A burn spell cast in
response to the creature resolves first and turns it on, which is what the rule says and what a
player expects. **An** opponent: any one seat other than the controller's, so in a pod it does not
matter whom you hit.

`CardScript.bloodthirst?: number` rather than a predicate on `entersWith`: the script stays data
(D364), and the engine owns what the word means.

### What is not read

- **`Bloodthirst X`** (two legal cards): X is the damage dealt this turn, not a number on the
  card. The reader takes digits only and the line stays reported (D259).
- **A bloodthirst creature that arrives without being cast** gets no counters, because the block
  that applies them runs on spell resolution. That is the gap task #397 already names for
  `entersWith` (Vanishing, Fading, Modular); bloodthirst joins the list rather than widening it,
  and the fix is one move for all four.

### Tests: one row per word of the condition

Bloodrage Vampire (3/1, bloodthirst 1) and Ghor-Clan Savage (2/3, bloodthirst **3**), rows copied
from the corpus, cast through the engine's own casting path. Nine rows:

1. no damage → no counter (the control; without it the rest prove nothing)
2. Shock an opponent → one counter, 4/2
3. two points of Shock turn on bloodthirst 3 → **three** counters, 5/6 — the number is the card's,
   and a reader that used the damage would make a 4/5
4. an ordinary unblocked combat hit, cast in the second main phase — how the keyword is played
5. Zulaport Cutthroat drains for one → life lost (asserted on `lifeLostThisTurn`), **no** counter
6. a Bears with Tainted Strike gives three poison → no life lost (asserted), counter **on**
7. City of Brass pings its own controller → damage this turn, to the wrong player, no counter
8. Shock on turn five, cast on the caster's next turn → forgotten
9. a three-seat pod, the Shock aimed at seat 2 and seat 1 untouched → counter **on**: *an*
   opponent, not the next one round the table and not all of them

Rows 5 and 6 are a pair that only the damage/life distinction can satisfy together; each asserts
the other record so that the missing or present counter cannot be explained by the event not
having happened.

Seven compile rows: the line reads on both printed cards and says N; `Bloodthirst X` does not;
the end anchor holds; the script carries `bloodthirst` and not `entersWith`.

### Measured

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| printed legal lines read | 23,689 | **23,710** of 56,421 (42.0%) |
| cards with a compiled script | 12,082 | **12,102** |
| cards with every printed line read | 7,903 | **7,917** |

+14 fully read, exactly the audit's prediction — the eighth reader row in eight for which it has
been exact. The other seven of the 21 print a second line something else has to read.

D557's pod sweep (SEED0=42701) finished while this was being written: 40 of 40 to a finish, no
throw, no stall.

## D559 — Fabricate, riot and unleash: a choice made as the permanent arrives

Three keyword rows on one cycle again (D557's arrangement), chosen as a batch because all three
are "the creature comes in and you are asked something", and the engine already had the question.

| keyword | rule | what it is | built from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Fabricate N** (CR 702.123a) | when this enters, you may put N +1/+1 counters on it; if you don't, create N 1/1 colorless Servo artifact creature tokens | a **trigger** | an `etb` trigger with one word-choice decision |
| **Riot** (CR 702.136a) | enters with your choice of a +1/+1 counter or haste | a **replacement effect** | the spell's own resolution `decisions`, read as the permanent arrives |
| **Unleash** (CR 702.98a) | you may have this enter with a +1/+1 counter; it can't block as long as it has a +1/+1 counter on it | a **replacement effect** and a **static** | the same, plus a `source-has-counter` static |

### The distinction the batch turns on

Fabricate goes on the stack. The creature is already on the battlefield when it asks, an opponent
may respond, and if they kill the creature the ability still resolves — and makes Servos whatever
was answered, because the counters cannot be put on and "if you don't" is what happened. That is
the keyword's own ruling, and it is why the effect checks where its source is rather than
trusting the answer.

Riot and unleash never go on the stack. A reading of either as an enters trigger would be a wrong
card rather than an approximate one (D362): a riot creature would be on the battlefield for a
moment without haste and without its counter, and an opponent could answer it in that window. So
the question is the spell's one resolution `decisions` entry — asked while the card is still on
the stack — and a new `CardScript.entersChoice: 'riot' | 'unleash'` tells the arrival block what
the answer means. It sits beside `entersWith` and `bloodthirst` and **adds** to them: Arcbound
Slasher prints modular 4 and riot, and is a 5/5 or a hasty 4/4.

Two fields and not one shared with `entersWith`, for the reason `bloodthirst` has its own: a
second line setting an already-set field is a field conflict (D487's whole-line rule), and the
Slasher's two lines would have refused each other.

### Unleash's static follows the counter, not the answer

"Can't block as long as it has a +1/+1 counter on it" is true of a counter from anywhere. So the
restriction is an ordinary conditional static (`while: source-has-counter`) rather than something
the arrival block switches on: a Cackler that declined and is later given a counter stops being
able to block, and one that loses its counter can block again.

The same shape is Chaos Imps' third line — "has trample as long as it has a +1/+1 counter on it" —
so that reader came along: `~ has <keywords> as long as it has a +1/+1 (or -1/-1) counter on it`,
in either word order. Only those two counters. A static keyed on a `divinity` or `shield` counter
nothing in the engine can place would be a line counted as read that never does anything.

### Riot's haste has no duration

The card gives it none. It is a permanent-duration effect whose source is the creature itself,
which lasts exactly as long as this object does and goes when it leaves (D304).

### The first option is the counter

`ChoiceDecisionSpec` documents the first option as the one a bot falls back on. For all three
that is the +1/+1 counter: a bigger body is never a wrong answer, haste is only right on a turn
the creature can use it, and a bot that cannot tell which turn that is should not guess.

### What is not read

- **A keyword granted to other permanents** — "Nontoken creatures you control have riot", "Other
  Dogs you control have unleash", "Other nontoken creatures you control have fabricate 1". Five
  cards, all reported.
- **Arriving without being cast.** The question belongs to the spell, so a riot or unleash
  creature that is reanimated or blinked is asked nothing and gets neither. For unleash that is
  the declined answer and is at least a legal game state; for riot it is a loss against the rules.
  Both join `entersWith` and `bloodthirst` under task #397, whose fix is one move for all of them.
  Fabricate is a trigger and is unaffected.

### Tests

Sixteen table rows on six printed cards (Glint-Sleeve Artisan, Weaponcraft Enthusiast, Zhur-Taa
Goblin, Arcbound Slasher, Rakdos Cackler, Chaos Imps), each cast through the engine's own plays:

- fabricate: the question is asked by a **triggered ability** with the creature on the
  battlefield; a counter and no Servo; a Servo (1/1, colourless, artifact, creature — each word
  asserted) and no counter; fabricate **2** on a 0/1 is two of one and never a split; and a Shock
  in response turns "counter" into a Servo.
- riot: the question is asked with the card **still on the stack** and leaves the stack empty;
  the counter makes a 3/3 with summoning sickness; haste attacks the turn it arrives and is still
  there on the caster's next turn; and both answers on top of modular 4.
- unleash: with the counter it cannot block; without it, it can; a counter added later turns the
  restriction on and removing it turns it off; and Chaos Imps' trample goes with the counter.

Twenty-one compile rows, including the three shapes that must stay unread for each keyword.

The first run failed on two rows, both the tests' mistake: the stack lives in `stackObjects`, and
a creature with summoning sickness makes the engine skip the declare-attackers step, so the row
that walked there found itself two turns later with a creature that could attack. That second one
is worth keeping as a fact about the harness: **`advanceTo('declare-attackers')` passes straight
through a turn in which nothing can attack.**

### Measured

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| printed legal lines read | 23,710 | **23,758** of 56,421 (42.1%) |
| cards with a compiled script | 12,102 | **12,140** |
| cards with every printed line read | 7,917 | **7,953** |

+36 fully read. The three keywords are 31 of those — fabricate 12 of 16, riot 8 of 13, unleash 11
of 14 — which is the audit's prediction to the card for the ninth, tenth and eleventh reader rows
running. The other five are the counter-conditional static.

D558's pod sweep (SEED0=42801): 40 of 40 to a finish, no throw, no stall.

### Break harness for D558: 13 of 13

Every break caught on the first run, each by the row written for it: life-lost in place of damage
by the Cutthroat drain, the unrecorded poison hit by the Tainted Strike row, the controller counted
as an opponent by City of Brass, "every opponent" by the three-seat pod, the damage used as the
count by the Savage's bloodthirst 3, and the missing cleanup reset by the next-turn row. The pod
row and the plain combat row were added after the first draft of the tests and before the harness
ran; the "every opponent" break is the one that would have got through without them.

## D560 — "Enters with N counters" applies to every arrival (task #397)

**The bug.** `entersWith` was applied in one place: the block that puts a resolving permanent
spell onto the battlefield. Every other way of arriving skipped it. A Zombified Arcbound Worker
came back a literal 0/0 and went straight to the graveyard; a Cloudshifted Calciderm came back
with no time counters and so never left; a reanimated bloodthirst creature was never asked. D558
and D559 each added a mechanic to that list and named the gap rather than widening the fix.

CR 614.1c makes these replacement effects on the *event* of entering the battlefield, and the
event does not care what caused it. In Commander, where reanimation and blink are staples, this
was the commonest way for a compiled card to be wrong while reading as fully read.

**The fix.** `arrivalReplacements(state, done)` in `automation.ts`, run from `settle` **before**
the state-based actions and again at the top of each of its passes:

- it walks `state.entered` — `relocate`'s and `createToken`'s own record of every arrival, which
  is the same "one place a card arrives" guarantee loyalty uses, one layer up where a script can
  be looked up;
- a printed number of counters is added there, and so is bloodthirst's conditional one;
- the spell path keeps only the **X** half, because CR 107.3m gives every other arrival an X of
  zero and only the resolving spell knows the number.

Before the state-based actions is the whole of the timing. The counters have to be there by the
time anything asks whether a 0/0 has toughness, and before the creature's own enters trigger is
put on the stack, since an intervening-if is asked as it triggers.

**What still asks nothing:** riot and unleash. Their counter is an answer, and a question needs a
resolving object to hang on (`pendingDecision.stackId`). A riot creature that arrives uncast gets
neither counter nor haste. That is now the whole of what remains of #397 and is written on the
player sheet as a stated limit.

**What did not change:** a board built before the engine takes over. Cards placed in setup never
entered — no enters trigger fires for them either — so the existing test that pins a setup-placed
Arcbound Worker dying as a 0/0 still holds, and its comment now says why that is the only way to
get one.

### Tests

Ten rows in "enters with counters, however it arrived (D560)", on pool cards and one printed
bloodthirst row. Run against the engine as it was before the change, **seven fail and three
pass**, and the three are the controls:

| row | old engine | new |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zombified Arcbound Worker has a +1/+1 counter | fail | pass |
| Zombified Calciderm has 4 time counters | fail | pass |
| Zombified Blastoderm has 3 fade counters | fail | pass |
| the Zombified Worker is a 1/1 and stays on the battlefield | fail | pass |
| a Worker with three counters, Cloudshifted, comes back with one | fail | pass |
| Calciderm moved by hand onto an automated battlefield has 4 | fail | pass |
| Zombified Bloodrage Vampire after a Shock has its counter | fail | pass |
| ...and with nobody damaged has none | pass | pass |
| a cast Calciderm has 4, once | pass | pass |
| a Zombified Endless One (X) has none and dies | pass | pass |

The full engine suite passed unchanged before any of these were written (3,542 of 3,542), which is
the evidence that moving the printed half out of the spell path changed nothing for a cast card.

No coverage change: this is a correctness fix for cards already counted as read. Its reach,
counted on the corpus: 57 legal cards print modular, vanishing or fading with a number, and 450
print some "enters with N ... counters on it" line with a fixed N. How many of the 450 the
compiler reads into `entersWith` today was not counted; every one that it does is covered.

D559's pod sweep (SEED0=42901): 40 of 40 to a finish, no throw, no stall.

## D561 — Kicker on a permanent: the declaration and its kicked line, read as one unit

The keyword audit ranks rows by cards finished *by reading the keyword line*, and kicker never
appeared near the top of it — because a kicker line is never the only thing unread. 247 legal
cards print one, and the line that says what the kick buys was unread on almost all of them. The
audit's ranking was hiding its largest row behind its own definition. Counted the other way, as
"cards finished by reading the pair", it is the biggest single row left.

**What was there.** Kicker has worked since task #45 for the pool's three instants and sorceries,
which read `ctx.kicked` while they resolve, and D423's `kickerSpellFor` compiles the two-number
damage family. Nothing read a kicker on a permanent.

**What a permanent prints.** Of the 103 legal permanents with a plain `Kicker {cost}`:

    When ~ enters, if it was kicked, <effect>.                                   59
    If ~ was kicked, it enters with N +1/+1 counters on it[ and with <kw>].      34

### The fact has to travel on the permanent

A kicked instant knows it was kicked for as long as it matters. A kicked creature's ability
resolves from the battlefield after the stack object is gone, so the kicked spell writes a
`KICKED` marker on the permanent as it resolves — evoke's arrangement, for evoke's reason. Like
any counter it goes when the permanent leaves, so a kicked creature that is blinked comes back
unkicked, which is the rule: the new object was never cast.

### The enters trigger is the existing reader's, with one clause taken out

"When ~ enters, if it was kicked, destroy target land" is "When ~ enters, destroy target land"
with an intervening-if in the middle. `kickerPermanentShapeFor` removes the clause, hands the
shorter sentence to `lineScriptFor` exactly as a card that printed it would be read, and puts the
kicked condition in front of whatever came back. So every effect the enters reader already knows
is a kicked effect — 35 of the 59 on the day this was written — and every one it learns later
becomes one with nothing to keep in step.

It insists on getting back **one self-`etb` trigger and nothing else**. The first version of that
check compared the event to `{ kind: 'etb' }` exactly and read none of the 59, because the enters
reader spells a card's own arrival `{ kind: 'etb', who: 'self' }`; the measurement after the first
build said "ETB 0, enters-with 29" and that was how it was found.

The condition is asked as the ability triggers (CR 603.4), so an unkicked Heartstabber Mosquito
puts nothing on the stack and **does not stop to ask for a target** — the test row that tells an
intervening-if from an effect that checks late.

### The counters are a second field, and D560 is why

`kickedEntersWith` rather than a conditional `entersWith`: D560 made `entersWith` apply to every
arrival, and only a spell can have been kicked. So this one is applied in the spell path beside
the marker, and a Zombified Academy Drake is a 2/2. The "and with haste" tail is a permanent
effect whose source is the creature, as riot's haste is.

### The declaration is never read alone

A `kicker` on a script is an offer: the table lists a second, dearer way to cast the card, and
the bot may take it. If the line saying what the kick buys were unread, that would be a way to
pay four extra mana for nothing — a card that reads one line short and plays as a trap. So the
reader returns nothing unless it reads both lines, wants exactly one kicked line on the card, and
on any refusal leaves the declaration reported as the unimplemented keyword it was (D362).

### What is not read

- the and/or family (`Kicker {2} and/or {1}{R}`, 18 cards), multikicker (19) and non-mana kickers
  (`Kicker—Sacrifice a land.`, 18): a different declaration each;
- 24 kicked enters effects the enters reader does not know yet;
- kicked counters with an X, a "for each", or a quoted ability for a tail;
- every kicked **spell** outside the two-number damage family (84 instants and sorceries,
  "do X; if this spell was kicked, do Y instead"). That is the next row in this family and a
  different shape: two effects in one resolution.

### Tests

Thirteen table rows on four printed cards, every effect run **kicked and unkicked**: three mana
or six for the Woodreaders and the two cards only when kicked; the kicked ability visibly on the
stack before the draw; a kick refused on three lands with the plain cast still offered; the
unkicked Mosquito asking for no target; the kicked one asking, and destroying; a kicked creature
blinked and not drawing again; the Drake a 2/2 or a 4/4; the Kavu with and without haste, and
still hasty a turn later; a reanimated Drake with no counters.

Eighteen compile rows, eleven of them refusals — and in each refusal **both** lines are asserted
unread, since reading the declaration without its partner is the failure this reader exists to
prevent.

### Measured

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| printed legal lines read | 23,758 | **23,886** of 56,421 (42.3%) |
| cards with a compiled script | 12,140 | **12,198** |
| cards with every printed line read | 7,953 | **8,008** |

+55 fully read, the largest keyword increment since the audit began, and the 8,000th card. 64
permanents now carry a kicker (35 by the trigger, 29 by the counters); the other nine have a third
line something else has to read. The probe before the work predicted 49 without the "and with"
tail and about 54 with it.

D560's pod sweep (SEED0=43001): 40 of 40 to a finish, no throw, no stall.

### Break harness for D559: 20 of 20

Twenty breaks across the three keywords and the counter static, all caught on the first run: the
fabricate answer ignored, counters put on a creature that has gone, one Servo for fabricate 2, a
Servo that is white or not an artifact, riot's haste handed to unleash, haste that wears off at
end of turn, a chosen counter that is two, the unleash static made unconditional or removed, and
the counter static reading any counter name or swapping its captures. 35 minutes for twenty
full-suite runs on two mirrors, with a gate and a pod sweep sharing the machine for part of it.

## D562 — A kicked spell with a second clause: also, or instead

D561's last "not read" item, taken next because it is the same family and the same rule: 84 legal
kicker instants and sorceries were unread, and D423's `kickerSpellFor` covers only the ones whose
kicked half is a second **number** ("deals 2 damage … it deals 4 damage instead").

Most are a second **clause**. The body is one printed line whose last sentence begins "If this
spell was kicked," and it is one of two things:

| | printed | kicked, the spell does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **also** | Return target nonland permanent to its owner's hand. If this spell was kicked, draw a card. | both, in printed order |
| **instead** | Target creature gets +2/+2 until end of turn. If this spell was kicked, that creature gets +5/+5 until end of turn instead. | the second, in place of the first |

The word "instead" is the whole difference and the reader takes it from the card and infers
nothing. Each wrong reading has a number in the tests: an Explosive Growth read as "also" makes
the Bears a 9/9, a Field Research read as "also" draws five.

### Both halves are read by the reader that already exists

`kickerClausePairFor` splits at the **last** "If this spell was kicked," and hands each half to
`spellScriptFor` as the one-line spell it would be on its own. Nothing about clauses is restated.
What it adds is three refusals, which are what make joining the halves sound:

- **Also: the kicked half may only be an effect** — exactly `{ onResolve }`. A kicked half with a
  target of its own (Jilt: "…kicked, it deals 2 damage to another target creature") is a target
  chosen only when the spell is kicked, and a script has one list of targets either way; reading
  it would ask for that target on every cast. A kicked half that asks a question (Runic Shot's
  scry) is refused for the same reason.
- **Instead: both halves must have the same shape apart from what they do**, compared as data —
  same targets, same flags, no questions. Tear Asunder exiles an artifact or enchantment unkicked
  and any nonland permanent kicked: two different things to point at, so it stays unread. So does
  "Counter target spell with mana value 2 or less … counter target spell instead".
- **Instead, with a referent.** "That creature gets +5/+5" is not a sentence a spell can open
  with, so "that creature" is replaced by the base half's own target phrase and the result read as
  usual. **The substitution is not trusted** — it is checked by the rule above, so a phrase lifted
  wrongly either fails to read or reads with different targets and is refused either way.

The base half keeps everything it read (targets, flags, questions) and only its effect is wrapped.

### What is still not read in this family

- kicked-dependent targets, both kinds above — this needs a second target list on `kicker`, which
  is a change to casting and to what `legalActions` offers, not to the compiler;
- "create four **of those tokens** instead", "search for **two** basic land cards instead of one":
  a count, not a clause, and a third shape;
- the kicked half that refers back without replacing ("that creature gets +7/+0", "those
  creatures also gain trample");
- and/or kickers, multikicker and non-mana kickers, as under D561.

### Tests

Seven table rows on printed Into the Roil, Explosive Growth and Field Research, each **kicked and
unkicked**, asserting the mana tapped as well as the effect — two or four for the Roil, with the
bounce happening both times and the card only when kicked; one or six for the Growth, a 4/4 or a
7/7, back to a 2/2 next turn; three or six for the Research, two cards or three.

Seventeen compile rows: six shapes read (including a three-sentence base and "instead" at the
front of the clause), nine refusals with **both** lines asserted unread, the base's targets shown
to be the unkicked spell's own, and D423's damage family shown to read as before.

### Measured

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| printed legal lines read | 23,886 | **23,916** of 56,421 (42.4%) |
| cards with a compiled script | 12,198 | **12,213** |
| cards with every printed line read | 8,008 | **8,023** |

+15 fully read. Eighteen kicker instants and sorceries now compile, up from three.

D561's pod sweep (SEED0=43101): 40 of 40 to a finish, no throw, no stall.

## D563 — The intervening-if in a trigger: D561's wrapper, given a vocabulary

D561 read "When ~ enters, **if it was kicked**, <effect>" by taking the clause out, reading the
shorter sentence with the reader that already exists, and putting the condition in front of what
came back. Nothing in that is about kicker. The same sentence shape, with any condition:

    When ~ enters, if you control an artifact, draw a card.
    At the beginning of your upkeep, if you control six or more lands, create a 5/5 …
    When ~ enters, if an opponent lost life this turn, each opponent loses 2 life and you gain 2 life.

Measured before writing anything: **334** legal trigger lines have a non-kicker "if" as the first
clause after the event and are unread; for **149** of them the shorter sentence already reads; and
**90** cards would be finished by it. The effects were never the problem. The conditions are a
long tail — the commonest is printed seven times — so this is a wrapper plus a vocabulary that
grows a row at a time.

### The wrapper

`interveningIfFromLine` sits in `lineScriptFor` **after** `triggerFromLine`, so it only ever sees
a line the trigger reader refused. It wants the prologue to hold no comma (so the "if" really is
the first clause, not "…, then if you control…"), a condition `interveningConditionFor` reads,
and the shorter sentence to come back as one trigger and nothing else. Any event will do — unlike
kicker, the condition is about the board and not about how the card arrived.

The condition goes on `TriggerDef.condition`, which the engine asks as the ability triggers and
again as it resolves (CR 603.4). That is what makes it an intervening-if and not a branch inside
the effect: a Scholar of Stars with no artifact puts **nothing** on the stack.

### The first vocabulary: four conditions, no new way of looking at the board

| condition | read from |
| --- | --- |
| an opponent lost life this turn | `lifeLostThisTurn`, spectacle's fact (D197) |
| you control N or more *things* | `countOfThing("<things> you control")`, plural |
| you control a / an *thing* | the same count, singular, at least one |
| there are N or more *things* | `countOfThing`, plural — creature cards in your graveyard, cards in hand |

Every count is D520's `countOfThing`, so "lands", "artifacts", "creatures", "other creatures" and
any subtype (Gates, Plains, a Dinosaur, an Equipment) come for nothing, with D521's correction
that a subtype counts permanents and not creatures, and with the plural rule that refuses Fungi.

Anything else is refused, and that matters more for a condition than for an effect: a condition
read loosely is a trigger that fires when it should not, on a card that reports every line read.

### Refused today, in the order they would be worth adding

1. "you cast it" / "you cast it from your hand" (40 lines) — needs a marker like `KICKED`, and most
   of their effects are unread too (4 of the 40 read);
2. "you control another <subtype>" — needs to know whether the card asking is one of the things
   counted, which a count alone cannot say;
3. "you control a creature with power 4 or greater" and other filtered counts;
4. "tribute wasn't paid" (11), "it was bargained" (6): each its own mechanic;
5. "you gained life this turn", "a creature died this turn", "you attacked this turn" — three
   per-turn facts the engine does not keep yet. `damagedThisTurn` (D558) is the pattern.

### Tests

Nine table rows on printed Scholar of Stars, Dragonmaster Outcast and Arrogant Outlaw, each
condition run true and false on boards that differ by exactly the thing it names:

- an artifact or a fifth Island — and with the Island the stack is **empty** after the spell
  resolves, not holding an ability that will do nothing;
- five, six and seven lands: none, one and one Dragon an upkeep, and the same again a turn later;
- no life lost; a Shock to the opponent (they go to 16, you to 22); and your **own** life lost to
  a City of Brass, with `lifeLostThisTurn['0']` asserted so the missing drain is about whose life
  it was and not about nothing having happened.

The first run of the land rows failed, and it was the tests: `start` walks to the main phase of a
turn whose upkeep the Outcast was already on the battlefield for, so a board with six lands
arrives with a Dragon. The rows now read that upkeep as the first observation and the caster's
next one as the second.

Seventeen compile rows: seven conditions read across three trigger events, the wrapped trigger
shown to be the shorter sentence's with a condition added and nothing else changed, and nine
refusals.

### Measured

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| printed legal lines read | 23,916 | **23,952** of 56,421 (42.5%) |
| cards with a compiled script | 12,213 | **12,243** |
| cards with every printed line read | 8,023 | **8,049** |

+26 fully read from four conditions; 34 cards carry a read intervening-if. Sixty-four of the 90
are still to come, each behind a condition on the list above.

D562's pod sweep (SEED0=43201): 40 of 40 to a finish, no throw, no stall. D562 also gained two
table rows and one compile row after it was pushed and before its break run: Bold Defense, for an
"instead" at the **front** of the kicked clause, and a refusal for two halves that each ask a
question.

### Break harness for D560 and D561: 19 of 21, and both misses were code that could not be reached

Twenty-one breaks on two mirrors in 36 minutes. Nineteen were caught by the row written for each.
The two that were not are the two I had marked beforehand as possibly unreachable, and they got
different answers:

| break | verdict | what was done |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D561: the event check in `kickerPermanentShapeFor` is dropped | uncaught | **removed.** The regex above it only accepts "When <this card> enters", so the shorter sentence can only come back as the card's own enters trigger. The check restated a fact already guaranteed and nothing could observe it. |
| D560: the per-pass `arrivalReplacements` call in `settle`'s loop is removed | uncaught | **kept, and labelled.** `settle`'s loop is written for arrivals that appear mid-loop, and the one thing in a pass that can produce one is a replacement's `instead`, which is an arbitrary script. No card in the pool has one that returns something to the battlefield, so no test can reach the line; a card that came back *instead of* dying would. The comment at the call now says "kept and unreached" in so many words. |

The difference is whether the unreachable case can become reachable without touching the guard. A
second test of a regex's own guarantee cannot; a hook for a script that has not been written can.

One catch was not a catch: "the arrival pass forgets bloodthirst" was reported caught **by the
type checker**, because the patch I wrote for it did not compile. That is a break that was never
run. It is in the next spec with a patch that compiles.

D563's pod sweep (SEED0=43301): 40 of 40 to a finish, no throw, no stall.

## D564 — What happened this turn: raid, morbid, revolt, life gained, and the ability word in front

D563 measured 334 unread intervening-if lines. That number was wrong by a factor of three, in my
own instrument: the probe only matched a line that **began** with "When", and only four events.
Counted properly — any trigger event, and with the ability word some lines print in front —
there are **1,046**, of which **176** sit behind an ability word, **385** have an effect that
already reads, and **249** cards would be finished. D563's own reader had the same blind spot, so
"Metalcraft — When ~ enters, if you control three or more artifacts, …" was unread although both
its condition and its effect were readable.

Ranked by cards finished, the conditions were not about the board at all:

| cards | condition | needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 17 | [Raid] you attacked this turn | a record |
| 12 | [Morbid] a creature died this turn | a record |
| 9 | you gained life / N or more life this turn | a record |
| 8 | [Revolt] a permanent you controlled left the battlefield this turn | a record |
| 7 | you control a creature with power N or greater (ferocious) | a filter |
| 4 | you're the monarch | nothing — `state.monarch` |
| 4 | [Metalcraft] you control three or more artifacts | only the ability word off |

### Four records, each written where the thing happens

`damagedThisTurn` (D558) is the pattern: optional on the state so an older save loads, written
in exactly one place, cleared at cleanup with the others, read through one helper (`turnFacts`).

| field | written by | the decision in it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attackedThisTurn[seat]` | `declareAttackers` | counts creatures **declared**; an empty declaration writes nothing, and a creature put onto the battlefield attacking was never declared (CR 508.4) |
| `creaturesDiedThisTurn` | `relocate`, battlefield to graveyard | asks whether the permanent **was a creature as it left**, from the state and instance before the move — last-known information (CR 603.10a). An animated land counts; an uncrewed Vehicle does not; a token does |
| `leftBattlefieldThisTurn[seat]` | `relocate`, leaving the battlefield | keyed by whoever **controlled** it as it left, which is what "you controlled" means and is not always its owner |
| `lifeGainedThisTurn[seat]` | `gainLife` | an amount and not a flag, because eleven cards ask for "N or more" |

### The vocabulary now

D563's four, and: you attacked [with a creature] this turn · a creature died this turn · a
permanent you controlled left the battlefield this turn (and the newer "left the battlefield
under your control") · you gained life this turn · you gained N or more life this turn · you're
the monarch · you have N or less / or more life · an opponent has N or more poison counters · you
control a creature with power N or greater · you control your commander.

`interveningIfFromLine` takes the ability word off first with the compiler's existing
`withoutAbilityWord`. An ability word has no rules meaning (CR 207.2c); the condition it names is
spelled out in the clause after it, which is the thing actually read.

### Refused, with the reason for each

Coven (distinct powers), "an opponent controls more lands than you", "you descended this turn",
"a nontoken creature died", "two or more creatures died", and any X. Each is either a comparison
this vocabulary has no row for or a narrower fact than the record keeps, and a narrower condition
read as the wider one is a trigger that fires when it should not.

### Tests: the recording through real plays, the comparisons asked directly

**Twelve table rows** on printed Mardu Hordechief, Cackling Prowler, Airdrop Aeronauts and Angelic
Accord. Each fact is made to happen by a real play and each has the row that tells it from its
neighbour:

- raid — no attack; an attack with the Bears; **a declaration of no attackers**; an attack last turn;
- morbid — nothing died; a Bears Shocked (one counter, still one a turn later); **an artifact
  destroyed**, with the graveyard asserted so the row is about what kind of permanent it was;
- revolt — nothing left; your Bears bounced; **an opponent's** Bears bounced, with the record
  asserted to be theirs;
- life — one Healing Salve is three and makes nothing, two is six and makes an Angel.

**Twenty-three direct rows** for the comparisons, where no play is needed: the condition is
compiled from the printed sentence and then asked of boards that differ by one fact — monarch
you / them / nobody; life 10 against 11 and 30 against 29; three poison on them, two on them,
three on you; a 3/3 that becomes a 4/4 and an opponent's 6/6; a commander that is yours, theirs,
in the command zone, or yours under an opponent's control; and a state with the four fields
missing altogether, which must answer "nothing happened" and not throw.

**Eighteen compile rows**: five ability words read, five bare conditions read, eight refusals.

### Measured

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| printed legal lines read | 23,952 | **24,047** of 56,421 (42.6%) |
| cards with a compiled script | 12,243 | **12,326** (40.1%) |
| cards with every printed line read | 8,049 | **8,122** |

+73 fully read, the largest increment of the session and more than any keyword row has given.
129 cards carry a read intervening-if, up from 34. Of the 249, about 150 are still to come.

### What the wrong first measurement is worth

A probe's regex is a claim about the corpus, and I reported its count as the size of the family.
It was the size of the part my regex could see. The check that would have caught it is cheap:
count the same thing a second, cruder way — here, every unread line containing ", if " — and see
whether the two numbers are within sight of each other. They were not: 334 against well over a
thousand.

The gate caught one stale refusal before this was committed (D516's kind): D563's compile row
"leaves a condition that needs a filter unread" used "a creature with power 4 or greater", which
this increment reads. Retargeted to "a creature with flying".

## D565 — One sentence, two events; and the question that found them

Two increments of intervening-if conditions were found by asking "for which unread lines does
the rest of the sentence already read?" The same question, asked of trigger lines with **no**
condition:

    unread trigger lines with no "if":                       8,728
    whose effect already reads behind "When ~ enters, …":    1,274
    cards that reading the event alone would finish:           630

So for one unread trigger line in seven, the effect was never the problem — the **event** was.
That is a different picture from the one the "most common unread openings" table gives, which
ranks by how a line starts and says nothing about which half of it is unread.

The events are a long tail (the largest finishes 18 cards), so this is the first slice of it,
chosen by one criterion: **both halves are already rows in `TRIGGER_SHAPES`**, so each is a line
in a table and no engine work at all.

| printed | events | lines read | cards finished |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Whenever ~ enters or attacks, … | `etb` self, `attacks` | 33 | 16 |
| Whenever ~ attacks or blocks, … | `attacks`, `blocking-creature` | 10 | 8 |
| When ~ enters or leaves the battlefield, … | `etb` self, `leaves` | 6 | 5 |
| Whenever a creature dies, … | `dies`, any creature | 12 | 6 |
| Whenever a creature an opponent controls dies, … | `dies`, `of: 'opponent'` | 11 | 6 |

The table has taken a list of events since D134 and each becomes its own `TriggerDef`, so "enters
or attacks" is two triggers saying the same thing. Three details that are decisions:

- **"Blocks", bare, is the batched event** (`blocking-creature`, D482): once per declaration
  however many creatures were blocked, which is what `blockTrigger` already uses for the bare word.
- **"Enters or leaves" has no settled zone** for the clause's own subject — a permanent that left
  could be in any of four — so `where` is null for the pair and a clause that needs one refuses.
- **A once-a-turn restriction on a pair refuses the line**, by the existing rule: two events are
  two records, and one printed ability must not fire once per kind.

"A creature dies" needed no new event: `who: 'any'` with no `of` is what "~ or another creature
dies" already meant. `of: 'opponent'` has been in the event type since D134 and no printed row had
asked for it.

### Tests

Eight table rows on five printed cards, each pair tested on **both** of its events — a row that
read only the first half would pass a test of the first half:

- Grave Titan: two Zombies on arrival, four after its first attack;
- Howling Golem: both players draw when it attacks, and again when it blocks, with the hands read
  around the block so the turn's own draw is not in the difference;
- Aven Riftwatcher: 22 life on entering, 24 after it is bounced;
- Moonlit Wake gains a life when your Bears dies and when theirs does;
- Malakir Cullblade gets a counter when their Bears dies and **none** when yours does.

Ten compile rows: six sentences read with their exact event lists, four refusals (the once-a-turn
pair, three events, a pair with a half that is not a row, a narrower death).

### Measured

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| printed legal lines read | 24,047 | **24,120** of 56,421 (42.8%) |
| cards with a compiled script | 12,326 | **12,377** (40.3%) |
| cards with every printed line read | 8,122 | **8,164** |

+42 fully read from five lines in a table.

### The queue this leaves, by cards finished

Each of these needs an **event the engine does not raise yet**, which is why they are not in this
increment: `~ is dealt damage` (18), `you cycle or discard a card` (10), `you cast a historic
spell` (9), `a creature you control attacks alone` (9), `~ deals damage to an opponent` (8),
`you cast an instant or sorcery spell that targets a creature` (8), `a creature dealt damage by ~
this turn dies` (7), `~ becomes untapped` (6).

D564's pod sweep (SEED0=43401): 40 of 40 to a finish, no throw, no stall. D564 also gained three
table rows before its break run: a permanent that left under your control but is **owned** by an
opponent (a record keyed by owner would get it wrong and no earlier row could tell), and the
next-turn reset for the departure and life-gained records.

### Break harness for D562 and D563: 21 of 26, and what each miss turned out to be

Twenty-six breaks in 46 minutes. Five were not caught, and they were four different things:

| break | what it was | what was done |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D563: "there are N or more" is always true | **a missing test.** The condition had a compile row showing it reads and nothing that ever asked it | three direct rows: two creature cards in your graveyard, three, four — with three in the *opponent's* graveyard throughout, which are not yours |
| D562: a referent the base never named is read anyway | **a second guard for a thing already guarded.** With no target phrase to substitute, the kicked half either fails to read or reads with targets the base lacks, and both are refused further down | the early return is removed; the rule that checks the result is the guard |
| D563: an "if" later in the effect is taken for the condition | **a guard nothing reaches yet.** Measured on the corpus: 29 unread lines match without the no-comma rule, and none of them would go on to read today, because their effects are unread | kept, with that measurement written at the rule. It is what stops each of the 29 being misread on the day its effect is learned |
| D562: the clause reader is tried before the damage family | **not a defect.** The two readers are disjoint: the damage sentence's kicked half ("it deals 4 damage instead") has no target and does not read as a clause | nothing; the order is immaterial and now says so here |
| D563: the wrapper runs before the trigger reader | **not a defect**, for the same reason: no line is read by both today | nothing; it stays after `triggerFromLine` for the stated reason, which is about a future overlap |

Also in that spec, with a patch that compiles this time: "the arrival pass forgets bloodthirst"
(D560) — caught by six rows, D558's cast rows among them, since the arrival pass is now the only
place bloodthirst is applied.

The honest summary of the two orderings is that a break which changes nothing observable is not a
missed catch, and the harness cannot tell the difference; I can, by asking whether any input
separates the two programs. For the reader orders none does.

## D566 — Damage as an event: three sentences the board cannot answer afterwards

The head of D565's queue was three prologues about damage, and none of them is a row in a table:
each needs a fact that is gone by the time anything could look for it.

| printed | why the board cannot say |
| --- | --- |
| Whenever ~ **is dealt damage** | a creature the damage killed is in a graveyard with its marked damage wiped |
| Whenever ~ **deals damage to an opponent** | a life total going down does not say what lowered it |
| Whenever a creature **dealt damage by ~ this turn** dies | who hit whom is not a property of either card |

So the engine writes damage down where it lands. `dealDamage` has one tail every landing of
damage passes through — after protection and prevention have taken their share — and it now
appends to two records: `damageDealt`, a transient list `settle` drains and announces, in the
same family as `died`, `entered` and `dealtCombatDamage`; and `damagedBy`, the turn's memory of
which object hit which permanent, cleared in the cleanup step.

Two new events and one filter:

| event | printed | lines read | cards finished |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `damaged` | Whenever ~ is dealt damage | 18 | 17 |
| `deals-damage`, `to: 'opponent'` | Whenever ~ deals damage to an opponent | 11 | 11 |
| the same, `who: 'attached'` | Whenever enchanted/equipped creature deals damage to an opponent | 3 | 3 |
| the same, `combatOnly` | … deals **combat** damage to an opponent (self, attached, "a creature you control") | 3 | 3 |
| `dies`, `damagedBy: 'self'` | Whenever a creature dealt damage by ~ this turn dies | 10 | 8 |

    printed legal lines read:            24,120 → 24,165 of 56,421 (42.8%)
    cards with a compiled script:        12,377 → 12,412
    cards with every printed line read:   8,164 → 8,206

Decisions, each of which is a rule rather than a convenience:

- **A creature the damage killed still gets its trigger.** The ability triggered when the damage
  was dealt; state-based actions buried the body afterwards (CR 603.2, 704.3). A Ripjaw Raptor
  draws for the hit that kills it. The watcher loop gained its sixth exception for this, for the
  subject only. `damaged` is offered to that one permanent and not walked across the board: every
  line read is about the permanent itself, and the event is raised for every landing of damage in
  every combat the bot simulates.
- **Combat damage in one step is one event** (CR 510.2). `dealCombatDamage` stamps everything it
  dealt as `combat`, and `settle` raises `damaged` once per creature for stamped records: a Raptor
  blocked by two Bears draws one card, where a Shock and a Bolt draw two.
- **"Deals damage" is an ability of a permanent.** A spell's damage raises no `deals-damage`
  event — the record says whether its source was on the battlefield — so a Shock at the opponent's
  face with a Thieving Otter in play draws nothing. (The record's flag is an economy rather than
  the reason: a spell in a graveyard is not a watcher either way. Written at the line.)
- **"An opponent" is asked from the watcher's seat**, so a ping at your own face is not one and a
  Curiosity on somebody else's creature answers for the Aura's controller.
- **A blinked object remembers nothing** (CR 400.7). A source is recorded as `id#objectSeq`, so a
  Sengir Vampire blinked after the bite is not credited with it; and a victim's entry is dropped
  when the card next enters the battlefield.

### A defect this found, which was not about damage

`addCounters` wrote onto whatever card had the id, wherever it was. "Whenever Fungusaur is dealt
damage, put a +1/+1 counter on it" resolving after the damage killed the Fungusaur put the counter
on the card **in the graveyard**, and `relocate` carries a card's counters onto the battlefield
with it — so the next Zombify returned a 3/3. Any ability that resolves after its source has died
had the same hole; this is the first printed line that walks into it every game. A +1/+1 or -1/-1
counter now goes only on a permanent. Time counters on a suspended card in exile are untouched.
Confirmed load-bearing: with the guard removed, the lethal-damage row is the one row of this
block's 22 that fails.

### A pool card that was narrower than its text

The pool's Thieving Magpie was written as "deals **combat** damage to **a player**", in both its
card text and its script. The Oracle text is "deals damage to an opponent". The two agree for a
bare Magpie, which is why nothing ever noticed; the compiled-against-written check noticed the
moment the compiler could read the real sentence. Text and script both corrected.

### Refused, with the reason at the row

- "Whenever **equipped creature** is dealt damage" (one legal card): a host the damage killed has
  been detached from by the time the event is raised, and `damaged` carries no list of what was
  on it. It would be right for survivors and wrong for the case that matters.
- "A creature dealt damage by **enchanted creature** this turn dies" (Vampiric Embrace, one card):
  its effect is "put a +1/+1 counter on **that creature**", meaning the enchanted one, and the
  effect reader binds "that creature" to the event's subject — the creature that died. Read, it
  would have compiled with nothing unread and done nothing. Found by reading the list of what the
  new rows read, card by card, before any test was written.
- A trampler that dies to its blocker in the step it tramples over should still get "deals damage
  to an opponent". `combat-damage` has never fired in that case either; the two are the same
  sentence and stay consistent. A known gap, written at the exemption.

Tests: 22 runtime rows on eight printed cards compiled from corpus rows (each sentence run both
ways — the wrong creature, the wrong player, a spell where the sentence says a permanent, combat
where it says any damage and the reverse, this turn and two turns later, both blinks), 16 compile
rows (nine readings, one "still on the old event", six refusals). Engine suite: 3,751.

The queue behind it, same instrument, re-run on this build: `an enchantment you control enters
and whenever you fully unlock a room` (10, eerie — half of it is Rooms, which the engine does not
have), `you cycle or discard a card` (10), `you cast a historic spell` (9), `a creature you
control attacks alone` (9), `you cast an instant or sorcery spell that targets a creature` (8),
`you expend N` (7), `~ becomes untapped` (6).

## D567 — Discarding and cycling as events; and what the cleanup step does not do

The next rows of the queue D565 built. Three families in one increment, because two of them
needed almost nothing:

| event | printed | triggers | on fully read cards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `discards`, by you | Whenever you [cycle or] discard a/another card | 20 | 16 |
| `discards`, by an opponent | Whenever an opponent discards a card | 8 | 6 |
| `discards`, by anyone | Whenever a player discards a card | 1 | 1 |
| `cycles`, by you | Whenever you cycle a/another card | 6 | 5 |
| `cycles`, by anyone | Whenever a player cycles a card | 4 | 4 |
| `cycles`, `self` | When you cycle ~ [or it dies] | 11 | 8 |
| `attacks`, `alone` | Whenever ~ / a creature you control attacks alone | 11 | 9 |

    printed legal lines read:            24,165 → 24,229 of 56,421 (42.9%)
    cards with a compiled script:        12,412 → 12,452
    cards with every printed line read:   8,206 → 8,258

**Discards needed no new record.** `relocate` has kept a `discarded` list since madness (#171),
because a card going from a hand to a graveyard cannot be told from a milled one afterwards.
`settle` now raises one event per card in it, with the discarding seat as the actor. A card whose
discard madness replaced is still in the list, and was still discarded.

**"Cycle or discard" is one event.** Cycling's cost is a discard, and the ruling printed with Drake
Haven is that the ability triggers once for a cycled card. So that prologue is the discard row with
two more words in it, and there is a row proving a cycled land pumps Hekma Sentinels once.

**Cycling needed a flag, in three places.** "Whenever you cycle a card" must not fire for a Mind
Rot, and it must not fire for a card that discards itself for some other effect — `discardSelf` is
also how channel is paid. So `AbilityDef` gained `cycling`, the activation that pays such a cost
writes the card into a new `cycled` list, and `settle` raises `cycles` from it. The flag had to be
set where a cycling ability is *built*, and there were three builders: the hand-written cycling
land, the keyword reader, and — found by the compiled-against-written check, not by me — the land
derivation in `fromCardData`, which builds its own. Without the third, a Barren Moor read from
printed data was discarded and never cycled.

**A card watches its own cycling from the graveyard.** "When you cycle Krosan Tusker, …" is an
ability of a card that went from a hand to a graveyard and was never on the battlefield. The
watcher loop gained its seventh exception, shaped like the stack's rather than the graveyard's: the
cycled card is offered the event as its own subject and may answer with its `self` cycle trigger
**and nothing else**. The row that pins it is a Drannith Healer ("whenever you cycle *another*
card") cycled with no Healer in play: it gains nothing, because a card in a graveyard is not
watching.

**"Attacks alone"** has been on the `attacks` event since exalted. Two table rows.

### What it found: the cleanup step has no priority round

A discard to hand size happens in the cleanup step. The engine ends the turn and then announces
the discard, so "whenever an opponent discards a card" goes on the stack in the **next** turn and
resolves in its upkeep. Megrim's damage lands a step late, which hardly matters; an "until end of
turn" pump from the same discard lasts through the opponent's whole turn, which does.

The rule is CR 514.3a: if anything triggers during cleanup, the players get priority in that
cleanup step and another cleanup step follows. The engine has never done this — its note on step
triggers says a trigger in a step without priority "waits for the next step that grants it", which
is the rule for the untap step and not for this one. It was unreachable in practice until a
printed line watched discards.

Not fixed here: it changes when madness is offered at cleanup and puts the bot in a step it has
never held priority in, and it wants its own increment and its own sweep. **Task #407**, next. The
row "fires for a discard to hand size in the cleanup step" asserts today's behaviour by name, so
the fix has to change it.

### Break harness for D564 and D565: 35 of 36

Thirty-six breaks in 64 minutes. One uncaught: with the owner check deleted from "you control
your commander", every row still passed — none of them put **somebody else's** commander on your
side of the table. A stolen commander is a commander you control and is not yours. Row added; it
fails with the break applied.

D566's pod sweep (SEED0=43601): 40 of 40 to a finish, no throw, no stall, in 4m53s — the new
per-damage events cost nothing visible.

Tests: 22 runtime rows on nine printed cards (each event for the seat it names and not the other;
a cycled card as one discard; a discard that is not cycling; a card that discards itself without
cycling; the cycled card answering only for itself; alone and in company), 20 compile rows.
Engine suite: 3,793.

## D568 — The cleanup step that holds priority (CR 514.3a)

D567 found it and this fixes it, the same day, because a printed line now walks into it every
game a discard payoff is on the table.

**What was wrong.** A discard to hand size happens in the cleanup step. `discard()` ended the
turn and *then* settled, so anything the discard triggered went on the stack in the next player's
turn and resolved in their upkeep. Megrim's two damage landed a step late. Worse, an "until end of
turn" pump from the discard — Hekma Sentinels, Flameblade Adept, the whole Amonkhet cycle — was
applied in the opponent's upkeep and lasted through their turn: a 2/3 blocker was a 4/5 for a turn
it should have spent as a 2/3. Madness offered at cleanup was offered in the wrong player's turn.

**The rule.** Normally nobody receives priority in the cleanup step. If anything triggers during
it, the active player does — in that cleanup step — and once the stack is empty and everybody has
passed, there is **another cleanup step**.

**What changed.**

- `discard()` settles *before* ending the turn. If that left something on the stack or a question
  open (`cleanupHolds`), the step holds: priority goes to the active player and the turn does not
  end. If nothing triggered, the turn ends exactly as it always has.
- Passing on an empty stack in a cleanup step runs the step again (`finishCleanup`): hand size is
  checked a second time, and only then does `endTurnCleanup` run and the turn move on.
- Between the first card of a two-card discard and the second, **nobody has priority**. This was a
  second defect, found by the row written for it: `settle` was handing priority to the trigger's
  controller with a discard still owed, so a Megrim could have resolved between the two cards. The
  discards are one event in the rules; their triggers wait for all of them.

**One divergence, named at the function.** The rule wears damage off and ends "until end of turn"
effects in the first cleanup step and again in the second. This does it once, at the end. A turn
later the two are indistinguishable; during the priority round itself a creature's marked damage
is still on it, which matters only to something that deals damage in a cleanup step to a creature
already hurt that turn.

Tests: seven. Megrim resolves in turn 5's cleanup and the turn then ends; a quiet cleanup is still
silent; the Sentinels are a 4/5 for the rest of turn 5 and a 2/3 in turn 6; priority is withheld
between discards; a card arriving in the round makes the second cleanup ask for another discard;
madness is offered in the cleanup step and resolves before the turn ends; declining it lets the
turn end. Engine suite: 3,799.

No card count moves: this is the engine doing what 29 already-read cards say.

## D569 — "From the battlefield" meant from anywhere, and a pod looped on it

D568's pod sweep (SEED0=43801) was the first in nine not to come back clean:

    Games: 40    finished 39    looping 1
    seed 43821: looping — 2000 moves with no progress in cleanup of turn 188,
                1000 of them auto:discard (Undying Rage)

**What it was.** Undying Rage: "When Undying Rage is put into a graveyard **from the
battlefield**, return Undying Rage to its owner's hand." The compiler had two rows for that
sentence (the solo form and Ichor Wellspring's "enters or is put into a graveyard from the
battlefield") and both emitted the bare `to-graveyard` event, which is Planar Void's — a card
arriving in a graveyard from **anywhere**. So an Undying Rage discarded from a hand returned
itself. So did one that was milled, or countered.

**How old.** D461 for the solo row, and the pair row since the table was first written. The
pool's own Rancor had it too, and its card text said "from anywhere" to match — so the check that
compares a hand-written script against the compiled reading agreed with itself.

**And Rancor was made wrong on purpose, which is the part to remember.** D179 is titled "Rancor
says 'from anywhere'" and changed a correct `dies`-shaped trigger into the wide one, on the
statement that "the card has read 'from anywhere' for years". It has not. The corpus row — the
Oracle text — is "When Rancor is put into a graveyard from the battlefield", and it was sitting in
the corpus the whole time. That sentence in D179 was written from memory and checked against
nothing, which is exactly what D259 forbids for numbers and nobody had thought to forbid for card
text. D179 and D172's table row stand corrected by this entry; the player cheat sheet, which
described the returning-from-a-discard as a feature of the deck, is corrected too.

**Why nobody saw it.** A card coming back to a hand a turn late does not look like anything. With
D568 the discard's trigger resolves in the cleanup step, the card is back in hand, the second
cleanup step asks for a discard again, and the bot discards the same card: for ever.
